tips.comment: good stable, although still a maiden at 7.y.o. this one has shown some promise this year over hurdles for the Jardine stable, finished 2nd and then 3rd in class 4 handicap hurdles at Musselbrough, this is a very weak class 6 event back on the flat, looks to have been found a good opening
Yet to win from 20 starts but has placed in 2 of ladt 4 outings. Can be slowly away but if getting away quickly has every chance of breaking that duck

Jumeira Vision has notable course and distance credentials, having won 50% of its races at this track and 37.5% over this distance. That indicates clear affinity for both elements, which is often a key factor in predicting success.

Has yet to hit top form this season, but is a 4 time C/D winner who has dropped to a lowly mark of 46 in this race. Good apprentice back up claiming 5lb and shrewd trainer is best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons @ 15 percent, making current 10/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Had two runs this season already which was desmal, but with those two runs under his girth could be focus enuff in a event of this nature, and turn the form around with this very good apprentice.
BLUFFERONTHEBUS is itching ever nearer to getting back in the enclosure and she has to be considered here. Trip going and weight all look manageable so she has sound claims and looks the one to beat.

Coma Cluster returned in April to a close second off a 69 but did not fair so well last time out when stepping up to 1m2f for the first time while on a 71 and I think the return to 1 mile today off a 70 could bring him back in
In excellent form, 2 ins and 3 places from five runs, so a proven consistent sort that will always try. Jockey is in excellent form and the ground will suit today. Big value on this ride today.
Havana Rum was second to Iris Dancer here last week who has taken on 4 lbs for that win and my pick could swap places as he stays on the same mark

Mullen takes the ride for Davidson, whose yard is in form. This mare knows Beverley inside out, with 7 course wins, including over this trip. Last time she got a bold front running ride and scored by a head here last week off 59 and still remains 7lb below her peak from last year. Drawn well in 3, she should be handy in a race lacking pace here
Inanna looks to be a decent option in this race, with the 1st two having come out of a run recently that turned into a bit of a battle between them. Think Inanna will be played late and can win this.

Dazy Mazy has run 12 times over this distance with 2 wins and 2 places, giving a 16.67% win rate and 33% place rate. She has shown ability on similar going with 1 win from 4 runs (25% win rate). In class 4 handicaps, she holds a decent record of 1 win and 3 places from 10 starts (10% win rate, 40% place rate). Draw in stall 4 is okay for this trip (a little higher than I prefer) but the trainer Mackie and jockey Waugh have her dropping 1lb below her last winning mark. The pace looks solid here, but she may struggle to win, so she is my each way chance today

Awaafi is a half sister to Kylian and if ready to go, she will take some beating in this field based on that pedigree. It's still a guess of who is most ready on the day, but purely on the horse's page this looks a great bet.

Karl Burke 2YOs at Hamilton - 20.4%SR, 47% placed, +£51.74 LSP to £1 EW Stakes. 2 winners from 4 runners in 2025 so far. Only cost 4000gns - Half-Sister to 3 winners. Bated Breath has had 8 Juvenile runners at Hamilton, 1 winner and 5 places from those 8. Tom Eaves - 19% SR for Karl Burke, 1.97 A/E, +£18.20 LSP to £1 Stake. Current Fav (Baggot Street) ran to an RPR 65 last time, so does not set an insurmountable standard.

Bona Fortuna was a close 5th of 20 at York over six furlongs on 31st May on his first run for 275 days. He lost two places late on at York and now tries the minimum 5f for the first time and he could win off the same mark against some previous winners up in the weights.
Has found some improvement this year and has won both of last 2 outings. Has gone up 12lbs but further improvement remains likely. Every chance of being there or thereabouts in hat trick attempt

Hurt You Never is 3 wins from 4 at this venue (only defeat was by 1.5 lenghts). Probably overpriced for this contest stepping up to class 4 after winning at class 5. Would need a career best to win this but can't be written off with fantastic course record
drops a further pound in the weights and wears visor for first time. hampered over a much longer trip last time and interesting back down to a mile here
Cymbidium was a close second off a 73 before the break in Oct and has had two runs to tune up since the return in April and could be ready now on a 71 with Kevin Stott this time

Had a 6f warm up three days ago and now steps up to the correct trip for the wily old, Group One Sprint-winning trainer who lets his horses do the talking, which is just as well, as no-one south of the border can understand a word he says!
Hasn't really had much luck in his career, but Obito does look better than a horse rated 72 and has to be able to put it up to this field

SAY WHAT YOU SEE is a three year old who looks capable from his current mark and his latest effort over today's course and distance offered hope he had come back to hand. Third-up for this spell with a high on confidence Paul Mulrennan aboard he will do.
Yet to win from 7 starts but has placed on 3 occasions. Likely to bounce back from a disappointing run last time but holds an each way chance

Gained valuable experience over C&D here last month in her handicap debut when she finished 6 of 11 and the expectation is that improvements will be made especially helped by a yard currently in good form.
Paper Doll is an intersting horse in this race, given the back class in Ireland. Looked to still have ability at Catterick on stable debut, but now has a good chance to go close again

When Ravenscraig Castle finished a very close third in the Melrose at York in 2021 it would have been inconcievable to think he would have failed to win another race. That has been the scenario, and here he is in a Class 6 handicap at Hamilton, and not even one of the more fancied runners. He has occasionally hinted that he can still win, and this is his very last chance for me. The ground should suit and the stiff finish may be just right for him to grind out the win.
10 times winner who has also placed on 27 occasions. A little disappointing last time but holds an each way chance if bouncing back
Ana Emaraaty from the Jim Goldie yard ran respectably here last time when fourth yard had a Royal Ascot winner yesterday this one could go close to giving them a winner here at Hamilton
Just held when runner-up over this trip at Carlisle on the 30th of May and will come on for that run following an absence of 178 days.

TORONTO RAPTOR is one of two that trainer Liam Bailey sends to Hamilton today. Both appear to have realistic chances possibly overpriced underestimated and this four year old's last run hinted he may have finally come to hand. Not long with this yard as a former Michael Bell trained runner well treated he appeals.

JAMINOZ drops below the weight he was for last season's peak and has been on the fringes on two runs so far this season. Considered if bouncing back and the fact he's eased in grade to face lesser opposition are another plus. This distance seems well within the remit so we could have one that gets involved.
I think CINDERELLAS DREAM is a live one that probably has further improvement in the offing. She'll run her race again for sure and I doubt a three pound penalty stops her.
Last race did confirm the ability held by One Look at a decent level, coming close to Porta Fortuna, who is a world class horse. Great chance here

On first appearances Fallen Angel was a bit disappointing on her first run this season at Newbury, but she ran similarly in her first race last season and then went on to win the Irish 1000 Guineas, so the indications are that she needed that run and could come on a lot for it. She is rated only 1lb behind the favourite and with a 3lb pull in the weights can make her presence felt.

Easy winner of this race last year and 2 runs this season will have them spot on to defend their crown. World class jockey who was on board for that win back up and master training duo who are tops here numerically last 5 seasons, best with their 4yo plus in same period @ 16 percent with a Lsp of 32.54, making current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.

At their collective best it looks to me like these are closer together on balance, and it could just be about which one turns up on the day. Elmalka looked a touch overpriced as a result, as at her best she is a at home as a Group 1 filly. She’s got a bit of form to turn round with the Godolphin Fav which is probably why she’s such a big price, but arguably she was in need of that run whereas Cinderella’s Dream was more race fit from exploits abroad. She took a step forward into Group 1 company in France finishing behind Sardinian Warrior who has had his Ascot run franked by Docklands. A strongly run mile on a stiff track should suit this horse, and the quick ground should also help her gain any ground late on. Stall 1 could prove problematic if she can’t get forward, but again the negatives looks baked into her price to give her a small chance.

Soprano beat Crimson Advocate who won next time out with the 2 reopposing today. Made all that day and this track over 7f suits prominent racers. Has won at this meeting before in the past and has each way claims
made a good effort on return from a poor position. has landed a good draw here and his form from last year is outstanding. Good value.

Yard have a great record in this race and Crimson Advocate was a 5 furlong, Group 2 winner as a 2 year old at Royal Ascot. Has shown decent mile form at Listed level this season. Conditions to suit and if still maintaining that sprinter pace should be competitive at the business end of the race.

LOS ANGELES going to be asked some questions here but looks a tough cookie and could well be able to see this out. Plenty of challengers have him as the target but this could be the O'Brien/Moore winner today
Very promising effort on return in Ireland. Was travelling much the best and only got tired inside the final furlong. will come on for the run and looks a strong player.

Map of Stars has drited out to a decent price following support for the top 2 in the market, but he looks to hold every chance here. His overall form is very good and he was arguably unlucky not to beat Sosie in France last time following 2 easy wins. He hasn't got much form on quick ground but he is by the brilliant Sea The Stars, so he should be effective on it.
Very taking race last time at York and you cannot ignore that and the money spent to supplement this horse for the race. Has to enter calculations.

The Gosden's train Ombudsman for the blue of Godolphin, with William Buick in the saddle. The son of Night Of Thunder finished 2nd returning from a long lay off on his seasonal debut 20 days ago to the 116 rated Almaqam which was his first loss in 5 starts. Should be match fit here and a big run is anticipated.

Facteur Cheval's record in Ascot Group 1 events is 262. At 25/1 I can't ignore this horse who has Group 1 winning form at Meydan on a sound surface. He has won in the month of June and can make the places.
The winner of the Wolverton at this meeting last year does show it comes to life at this time of year..could go well if some falter and is juicy odds if extra places are up for grabs

Continuous is obviously the pacemaker for Los Angeles .(to be honest I don't see the need) who is trying to repeat his win last time v Anmaat who may well be up to full fitness now.I am at a loss to see this being slowly ran and if it is Continuous if making the pace could cause a massive upset and hold on.

TRUE LOVE represents leading trainer , owners and breeders and presumably a great deal of thought would have been given to the right race tactics for this juvenile filly stepping back down to a stiff five furlongs. A high draw over the straight sprint course at this meeting in big fields has played out well in years gone by , so hope is high.

Fallen Angel is a 4yo is 4/9 wins and a winner of last years Irish 1000 Guineas - she handles today good to firm ground and should go well today in first time cheekpieces under James Doyle for Karl Burke who is 999 wins from 7411 runners in first time headgear.

SOCIETY KISS is by a sire who won a Royal Ascot sprint and trainer Ralph Beckett understands exactly how to bring a filly forward. Her only start to date was a course and distance win which stacks up well and potentially seen to even better effect second-up she makes each-way appeal.

On what looks an extremely competitive Wednesday here at Ascot I'm throwing a couple of darts in most races. The Michael L W Bell trained Spicy Mag has one of the best speed ratings in the field when a 3l winner in a Cl2 novice at Newmarket on debut quickening clear nicely.
With Osin Murphy riding, Cardiff By The Sea makes some appeal as an each way shot In a race of this nature, With one run to his name Cardiff By The Sea could be the unknown factor here.

A 2yo lottery so land somewhere if you want a play, and one that I liked was Staya who won on debut with minimum of fuss and in a fair time. She looked to be well within herself there and could have won by much further. A low draw is a slight concern, but she appears to be drawn around some strong pace angles which will hopefully have her forward enough to get involved at the sharp end.
Won in fine style in the U,S in it's last race, and they wouldn't be sending one over here for just a run out, and at 14/1 it's got to be seriously considered, e/w advised.
Harry's Girl is regarded highly by the Hannon yard and they know how to get these 2yo horses prepped for the big ones. Willing to take a chance EW at a lovely price

Lots went wrong for Revival Power on debut, but she miraculously managed to win. She must have been at least 10 lengths behind the leader after the first furlong, a position from which I've never seen a debutant win. Tim Easterby his interview after the race was very interesting, as he said they hadn't trained her too much yet and he immediatly mentioned she was going to Royal Ascot. He's had some decent 2yo s in his time, but doesn't bring them to the Royal meeting unless he thinks they have a chance. I'm interested to see how she'll run.
Secret Hideaway ran on well to lead near the post after being slightly hampered at the start at York last time. She could do well at Ascot, drawn just higher than the favorite.
Travelled much the best last time in a Listed race after doing all the donkey work. Has definitely enough ability to run a race of this nature and could play a major role if able to settle.

Won a low grade filly novice race at Kempton in good style and was drawing further and further away at the finish and showed a good attitude. Obviously expected to win that day as sent off 4/7 fav. Needs to step up and not badly drawn in 21.
I'm taking a chance that this filly can improve enough to figure here for her up and coming in form yard. Colin Keane takes the ride which looks significant.

Despite looking up against it in this company, JUSTICE TWICE wasn’t as well positioned as the winner when 2nd to Guernsey Lady in a Novice Stakes at Lingfield 2½ weeks ago. She has placed three times in three runs (100%) on good-to-firm or similar going & has placed once in one run (100%) here at Ascot. Livey outsider.

The American horse drawn 13 is likely to burst out the stalls being a 4.5f winner and could well give this one a good tow drawn 11. Won her debut run at Redcar even though she ran green when asked for effort. Won nicely enough in a decent time and sure to improve for experience.

very competetive looking queen mary stakes where it might pay to look for a low drawn runner (going stick suggests this part of course is quicker) eskimo pie looks a great each way bet at a mouth watering 80/1.she has met trouble in her 2 runs to date but looks a promising sort and is drawn well in stall 3

A Space Blues filly, half-sister to the impressive 5f/6f Stay Smart. Her Dam was a 2-year-old winner at 7f and successfully competed at a distance of 1 and a quarter mile. Although the debut presents a challenging scenario, trainer Dylan Cunha's stable is currently thriving, and with 25 horses vying for position over 5f, anything is possible. The enticing odds of 150/1 make for a compelling each-way bet.
Rogue Legend does set the standard in this race and comes here with a stellar chance you would think. Has been bought by conections and this is a great chance for Ascot glory.

Two starts for the 2yo colt. He ran a nice race on his debut, only beaten very late on by an experienced and smart looking Appleby trained runner. Never troubled when winning a £26K conditions race four weeks ago - good RPR rating - and should be peaking at just the right time in this Listed contest.

The main reason that I am nominating Rogue Supremacy as my tip is due to the trainer who has been in great form recently, Rogue Supremacy was an odds on winner last time out and looks a runner still improving.

Havana Huricane 2 year old bay colt. Left a favourable impression when winning his racecourse debut, then finished second at Epsom when slowly away made up a lot ground very quickly but had nothing left towards the finish. Back down in trip should suit this colt.

UTMOST RESPECT ran on debut with great credit given how much went wrong. He looks like one of many potential big improvers now second-up in his career and drawn high in the sprints on quick ground at this meeting most recent years has been an advantage.

Won on his sole run at Keeneland over 5.5f 55 days ago on firm so should relish the surface which should quicken up as the day goes on . US horse have decent record in 5f races I think this one can bag a placed if getting nabbed late on .

Throw a dart, and I’ll chance Azizam here who went well on debut, travelling strongly and extended clear nicely. You could say the same for plenty of these, but he looks drawn well on the high side here to make use of the stands side rail with Kansas a non runner. He hung left having gone from right to left at Hamilton, but the rail should keep him straight and true here, and he could prove good enough to mix it in this company.
Not suited by the step up in trip over 6 furlongs at The Curragh last time out and this drop back to 5 furlongs appeals.

Very eyecatching how Richard Hughes runner had a tremendous turn of foot on debut at Leicester and that uphill finish was brushed aside with ease.you cannot take that away despite the opposition..Billy Loughnane rides and it looks interesting
Jan Steen had headwind and a penalty to deal with at York, he still ran a credible third and I can only see him improving on the stiff 5 furlongs.

Dickensian will need to settle better today because lto over c & d he was too eagre and got swomped in the closing stages. Having said that, he ran a similair race on debut which he won and i'm hoping it was just the fact that those races were just 14 days apart. Hopefully he's now fully charged for the trainer who won this last year.

Sovereign Spell looks a decent each way price at 33/1 with four places on offer. This is based on his neck defeat, despite running green, in a Newmarket novice event in May. The first and third placed horses both won next time. It looks like good form on a fast surface at today's distance. Rossa Ryan takes over in the saddle.

Gorey Gold has an excellent pedigree, sired by Galileo Gold. In his two previous races he has finished fifth and won once. He beat his nearest rival by more than 4 lengths in his winning race at Bath 12 days ago. His good form should not go to waste and he has a real chance of a podium finish
Logi Bear was out of luck in running last time out but previously won well at Newmarkert over six furlongs and can give a good account here under a positive run from Sean Levey.

Overpriced at 50s. Strong run 5f will suit as he won over 6f last time. Still green in winning that race, this is only his 3rd race and improvement is highly likely. He is rated 4th best on TF ratings in the race and is worth an ew bet
Too big a price would like extra places for a bet but tipped because ran well at big meetings always a slow starter but can keep on big ask but could show in speculative tip.
The layers have dismissed his win up at Ayr it seems and it was not the strongest of races but he did it very well and should improve again. I'd give him an ew squeak here under Colin Keane.

Despite this looking too tough, CALL ME BY MY NAME didn’t get no favours from the front runner when 3rd to Tricky Tel in a Novice Stakes at Chester 2½ weeks ago. He has placed twice in four runs (50%) on good-to-firm or similar going & has also placed twice in four runs (50%) for trainer James Horton. Lively outsider.

Has 1 win and two second place finishes from 3 career starts in France the last one a close second in a Group 3 at ParisLongchamp last month. Improving with every run and represents powerful connections so a big run expected with the step up in trip likely to suit.
Carmers last race is starting to add up quite nicely, with a couple of subsequent winners already, and looks to be the one most likely to get this trip, without question marks. Good opportunity here.

None of these have tried this trip (1m6f) but Shackleton won over 1m1f as a 2yo at the end of September, a long distance for a 2yo and suggests he will be a stayer. Had a prep run over 1m2f at the Curragh last month, getting outpaced in a Group 3 contest. Looks a fairly weak race.

This looks a really open race that lacks an outright potential superstar, and whilst he didn’t look like he wanted to go up in trip Pinhole takes a fair hike up here. The form took a major boost, and he wasn’t completely disgraced on reappearance behind the subsequent Derby winner and placed horse. He is a full brother to Cadogan Place who has placed over 2 miles, and there’s some fairly smart staying horses in both codes on the dams side, including a horse that stayed further than 3 miles on Gf ground. In a race where I found it tough to find a standout, I was happy to forgive him not taking to Chester and coming on for the run.

Ran a good 2nd of 8 last time out in a class 3 over 1m 3f 188yds on good to firm(ish) at York after being a bit keen early and then staying on the same pace at the finish. Extra furlongs today will suit after hopefully settling better under the same jockey.

Fallen Angel is a 4yo is 4/9 wins and a winner of last years Irish 1000 Guineas - she handles today good to firm ground and should go well today in first time cheekpieces under James Doyle for Karl Burke who is 999 wins from 7411 runners in first time headgear.
Stayed well when won on return after beiing stepped up in trip. Second pick from the Ballydoyle squad but this combo jockey/trainer won the Epsom Derby and looks sure to stay. Big player.

The Crisfords trained Spinning Wheel won a novice lto at Yarmouth over 11 1/2f by a short-head making it 2-2. The form of his debut win at Redcar has been franked since. More to do here but place chance.
Worth a little E/W punt here, has run on into fourth a couple of times in listed company and shorter distances and the extra distance should help here, could land another place

Did the business winning at Chester last month but going into the unknown now going up in trip and also makes course debut how drop down in class should help but will need to improve from LTO effort at Epsom this month.

James Owen might have the out sider here, but he can have one ready to run a very good race, which could see Hallelujah U with Jim Crowley in teh saddle sounding out a very good run. Won over twelve furlongs at Thirsk in a handicap, this is a big step up in class, which he can be shining through with being a colt by Pinotuba. 80/1 is a massive price, but he is in a field of a lot of ifs and buts with staying and a shock may not be a surprise, as James Owen has had 59 winners so far this season on the flat, at present time he can send the cat out and that could easily win. The Gredley Family are no strangers to winning big races and more than likely be here to see their horse run.

In her career, Rainbows Edge has raced four times, winning three and finishing second in th eother. Last month she won over today's course and distance, so taking her to do the same agin today, with the same jockey William Buick on boad.
This looks like a wide open race and I fancy the chances of Sky Safari who has already won a few good quality races and with what looks like being a good inside draw should have a good chance.
Arolla got eye-balled in the run in at a listed race at Musselburgh and still managed to finish with a kick that was impressive given the battle that had precluded it.

Going by last year's result on good to firm, the first two home in this race were 4 lengths ahead of the 3rd horse and they were lightly raced 4 years old near the bottom of the weights and both drawn high. Serialise drawn 24 meets all those credentials and she also has experience in large fields unlike most of these, when finishing 2nd and 3rd at the curragh and Leopardstown over today's distance. The price of 8/1 is shorter odds than what I would normally do in fields this big but It looks a great e/w bet with 6 places on offer, and should at least recoup losses with a small profit should she doesn't win.
A consistent type for trainer Charlie Johnson and although a beaten favourite last time here at Ascot that run was much improved and can come from off the pace with Jamie Osbourne aboard.

I'm targeting the other race on the card with 6 places on offer with value again the order. This time I've sided with the Northern raider Julia Augusta from David O' Meara's yard. My selection will appreciate competing against her own sex after a very promising first start of the year at Epsom over 8.5f when 3rd of 10 (beaten by the boys). That was after a 205 day break so is entitled to strip fitter here and with the yard jock Danny Tudhope getting the leg up I'm quietly confident of a decent show. This is a handicap like the Epsom start, but last season had been competing in listed/group level class.

Andrew Balding's 4 year old Blue Point filly is stepping up to a mile on turf. Race conditions to suit and a consistent performer in this grade albeit over a shorter trip. Has proven place form in big fields and on breeding shouldn't be phased by the extra distance today.

Snellen won on his sole course visit on his 2nd career start. Good win strike rate with 5 wins from 17 runs and 3 places. Campaigned in Bahrain leading in to this and has to carry 2nd top weight. Trainer is no stranger to big festival wins on the flat and hurdles. High draw won't be an issue and has place chances at minimum

Going to have a very speculative punt on a small trainer in Gemma Tuttys Thelmas Angel?....shes booked the very good Rossa Ryan here and for some reason too me its short enough in the betting at around 22/1?..on all firms..would be a miracle if it won but someone seems to fear it at the moment..gl to the connections ..small ew

With bookmakers paying six places, I’ve been looking for something at juicy odds that could run into the frame. Rose Prick is another consistent filly for Ed Walker who has progressed steadily in handicaps and arrives here in decent form, coming off an excellent Listed third at Nottingham. That was only her second run of the season, so she should strip fitter for today. She went close over this course and distance last year before running well in defeat when travelling to France, and the return to this stiff mile could play to her strengths. Worth a small each??'way play at 22/1.

Ambiente Amigo is dropping back in distance here, having run at up to 14f last season and then hurdling in the NH season. Her last three runs were at 10f at Listed and Group 2 level. James Owen makes use of apprentice Elizabeth Gale, who was a lightweight NH jockey and has recently been in good form on the flat as well. Drawn low in stall 3, there is likely pace far side from Arolla, Arisaig, Kayhana, and Sky Safari.

A chance is taken as Francophone is dropping back in trip which looks suitable as he hasn't really been seeing out the extra two furlongs despite winning over that distance. Eye catching the Christophe Soumillon takes the ride. Also has the application of cheekpieces which may just help. On a handy mark when looking at peak figures and could go well.

Changed my mind on my other tip for this race and have gone for this Irish raider. Seasonal debut over a mile was decent enough (7th/27) and won lto, again over todays 8f. This race is going to be tough, but like my ew tip, i feel this horse has improved and has chances. Ew for betting.
Upped to a mile here ROCKYMOUNTAINWAY could go well under a light weight. Never far away in fillies handicaps it is possible she may be seen to best effect up in trip.

Demonstrated the advantage of a comeback run by winning a 7 runner handicap at Leicester just 23 days ago. Although that race wasn't particularly challenging, it may not be the best indicator for success in a more competitive setting. Nethertheless, with both trainer and jockey performing exceptionally well, the 33/1 odds present a significant opportunity for profit with an each-way bet.

A few i like in here and one was Sky Safari, but the price has already gone on that one, so my ew tip will be Viennoise. Won lto for first victory and looked a much better horse than previous runs, but that's David O'Meara for you. Up 5lb, but that's offset by 5lb claimer and although this is tougher, i believe she will run well.
Bint Al Daar was 2nd of 86 earlier this year and won in June last year. She runs off 84 today and may outrun her odds.
Has some decent form in the book and gets weight off the more fancied runners. Interesting taht connections reach for cheekpieces could well get a place at rewarding odss

The Richard Spencer trained Shallow is not from one of the 'sexy yards' but the 81 rated filly does have the best speed rating in the field and has 4 wims and 4 places from just 10 runs. Only 24 runners this time go to post for the Class 2 Fillies' And Mares' Handicap. Today's jockey Hollie Doyle has the script: she can press the button, bounce him out from stall 14 and lead all the way...simples !

I have been with this horse for some time and like to stick with him as I see him developing into a Group-level performer in the future. He has been given plenty of time to mature, making his racecourse debut only at three years old, but already showing plenty of class. He broke his maiden when stepped up to a mile on the all-weather, romping home by 13 lengths before scoring again at seasonal reappearance in a canter over this course and distance. Upped 10 pounds since then, and despite a slow start, he needed every inch to beat subsequent Nottingham winner Boyfriend last time out at Newbury. Another 5-pound penalty won’t make things easier, but the stiff finish and a wide draw will play to his strengths over this straight course. Worth following at around 9/2.

The Balding & Murphy combination are in fine form of late and are hard to overlook with the King Power Racing owned Fox Legacy. Only had 8 starts winning twice and runner up once. Twice ridden on the all weather when unplaced and twice finding 12f a distance too far. Moved from the all conquering Sir Michael Stoute yard on his retirement and on seasonal/yard debut he won very nicely on the drop back to 9f. They will go flat out for this mile, so the ability to stay slightly further can help and with 6 places on offer he looks an outstanding each way touch.
Sent off 5/1 fav for the Victoria cup here at Ascot in May but got chinned on the line. Has good ascot form and has a good turn of pace and must be a solid place option at 10/1.

The Liffey is the most unexposed horse in the field. He had three runs for A P O'Brien, winning two of them, but was then gelded last summer and switched to Joseph O'Brien. Returning after 350 days off, unfancied in a 7f Listed race at Naas, finishing a never nearer 4th. Ryan Moore takes the ride, which is a hint in itself.

Bullet Point can go well in this ultra-competitive Hunt Cup. He has won his last 3 races comfortably and gone up the weights accordingly, but he looks like a large imposing horse who should be able to take on the extra pounds without too much impact. His sire is Advertise who won the Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot and also finished second in a big field in the Coventry, so he has a nice profile for this.
Arabian Light has only had six runs but has won three of those and placed in the others and with a good return last month to a third I think he could improve on that now second up EW 6P

EPICTETUS is by Kingman a sire who produces many who perform well at this meeting. This Ex-Gosden trained racer is beginning to look well treated and there was something to like about his seasonal reappearnce. With that run likely to have set him straight and Saffie Osborne riding the straight course better than many this five year old possibly now at his peak could have a say.

Back home after an indifferent spell in America and new connections have booked Christophe Soumillon which is perhaps a tip in itself. Every chance if anywhere near his best but does need to leave that American form on the other side of the pond.
Tony Montana ran a great race in his only previous outing over todays trip so with ideal ground conditions today may well be hard to beat.

In the each way market, this is perhaps a risky proposition given his recent form, but I can’t resist having a small interest in Ancient Rome. Previously trained by Andre Fabre in France and clearly well regarded, he showed decent form for his new yard last season, including a runner-up effort in a Group 2 over this course and distance. He also ran a strong third in a Group 1 at Colonial Downs before finishing a respectable fourth in the Darley Stakes. This year, he has yet to fire, finishing well beaten in three starts, including at Group 1 level. However, his handicap mark has dropped quickly as a result, and if he has built some fitness since his run at Newbury in May, he could bounce back now dropped into handicap company. Jamie Spencer, who excels on the Ascot straight course, is back in the saddle, and that could make a real difference. At around 22/1 with bookies offering six places, I’m happy to take a small each way chance.
Tokenomics was immediately pinned for Ascot after winning over this distance after having to sit and suffer for a run through during the race. Good each way chance

A lack of front runners across the field draws the eye to the forward goers, and whilst Silawi is well in under a penalty here I do wonder if he can just set this up for Sisyphean to settle off of him with the pair drawn alongside each other. Just a 2lb rise for his 2nd last time where he travelled sweetly into the race at York but got headed late on. He can come on for that career best effort first time up and hopefully the front runners can snatch a lead here and prove hard to peg back.

Possible question mark for URBAN LION is if he can turn it around quickly after the win at the weekend but I think if connections are happy and let him run then I'm happy to have some chips down as he's clearly improving and could have more to find.

I don't know too much about this one other than it's form in France last year was pretty decent. I believe it's now based in Qatar and has had just the one run for them back in February, but have not seen that race. Form from France imo should be good enough to compete here today if fit and ready and that's the risk here and why it's 33-1 and my win bet.

Won the Spring Cup @ Newbury and tends to run these mile handicaps very well. Retains a decent mark of 97 here, is a C/D winner and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 25/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Made all over a mile and a quarter at Windsor last time out on good to firm ground. Might have gone under the radar here if getting to the front in today's much bigger field. Handy middle draw and looks a massive price for each way purposes with James Doyle taking the ride and with many bookies paying out on extra places

Distance winner who had two runs in May finishing decent a 3rd place in both in class 2's over just short of 1m. Todays fast ground will suit under usual jockey and could be nicely drawn high in stall 18. Is ew price but ew bet on other selection.

The 5yo has not been over-raced but he can be a little hit or miss. Useful on his day, placed in both a Group 3 and Group 1 race previously. Back from an 8 month break with a nice run last month and hopefully he can build on that effort, a close 2nd or 13 in the decent Thirsk Hunt Cup handicap, posting a big RPR rating and he runs off the same mark in handicap. He was rated 10lb higher at the start of last year.
A consistent sort in these races and always gives a good running in them. Had nice run on seasonal debut in victoria cup which will have blown away the cobwebs and has ew possibilities.

4-Y-O distance winner who has been given a refreshing 81 day break since finishing a good 4th of 22 only beaten 1 1/2L in the Lincoln over 1m on good to soft. Had been kept busy before that with five runs in Meydan. Rating goes up to 97 from 91 but a good 5lb claimer takes over the reins. Fast ground okay as has a win on good to firm and is drawn in the middle in stall 16.

Runner-up twice over further last month before disappointing at Epsom over their extended mile when last seen where the undulating track may not have suited. He is 8 times a winner in a 62 race career, with 5 of those wins over this trip and could be each way value at a decent price.

A huge price to get amongst the 6 places on offer. Decent trainer and decent jockey, the right age, matches profiles of previous winners in pedigree and RPR ratings, drawn in 24 is not a bad thing and will have the stamina when plenty have cried enough. Always a big bonus at this stiff track. Loads of plusses for a 100/1 shot

One of the great cavalry charges and I have two hopeful selections, one drawn in the centre and Whip Cracker who exits stall 33. This horse took a step forward in the Lincoln Trial at Wolverhampton in March but then disappointed in a couple of outings back on turf. There was a revival in May when a keeping on second in the Whitsun Cup at Sandown. First time cheekpieces were worn and these are retained. Whip Cracker never showed over course and distance a year ago but, on his best form elsewhere, I have to give him an each way chance at 66/1 with six places.

Finished 4th in the guineas in 2023 went to Australia at the end of that campaign before returning this year and Finished an encouraging 5th in the Lincoln on his reappearance. Didn't run quite as well at Newmarket last time out possibly not staying, drops back to the mile here and the angle I like is he has been kept away from Firm ground since he won on it as a 2 year old , this being the first time he has run on ground with firm on it since then

It is easy enough to look elsewhere but SEAN could bounce back to form in this larger field, after finishing 5th (of 5) to Socialite at Windsor 3 weeks ago. He has placed three times in eight runs (38%) over 1 mile & has placed once in two runs (50%) here at Ascot. One to watch.

Toimy Son was noted making headway and keeping on at Royal Ascot two seasons ago when he raced in the 7 furlongs Buckingham Palace Stakes, finishing third of six in his group. That trip was not far enough as he showed when an excellent third of 31 in the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket in September. A big field and straight track suits. Toimy Son has won on fast ground. The horse has been ridden by an apprentice in both outings this season but today he is partnered by the in-form Callum Shepherd.

Rocks Up Late has won his last two chases at Worcester and Fontwell from the front and could win a third here at Worcester again unless Jaipaletemps improves considerably from his latest run at Ffos Las.

The model I run suggests a wide long shot Rathmacknee can cause an upset here and is the value bet. Rathmacknee showed some promise before losing form and then going on an extended break. First run in 108 days but lines up here with by far the highest RPR out of the 7 runner field. Has got the official ranking that is also the highest, but doesn't look overly penalised for it in the weights. Only carries ~6-8 lbs more on average than the other runners here, and Tabitha worsley relives 3lbs off that difference for claiming. There is very little form in this opener apart from Rocks Up Late, who is already a very short price of 4/6 and offers absolutely no value. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Awkward under pressure, aided by sole rival falling late won a novice hurdle at Ffos Las by 24| last time; steadily progressive and 3-3 over hurdles; trainer in form; can continue unbeaten run off lenient opening mark. Was declined an NR yesterday and entered here today so connections must think it has a better chance here.

The model I run suggests Scintillante can cause an upset and win this one. Scintillante lines up here with a comparable RPR to the rest of the 7 runner field but goes out carrying significantly less weight over this 2m 4f rond trip. the weight differential is 1 stone 7 lbs to top weight Heretoeternity and a similar margin to Sir Galahad who lines up here having won a string of recent results and is the in form horse. Scintillante is a prior course and distance winner, and was a reasonable 3rd when last out only 13 days ago. Now lines up at favoured left hand track again, and looks to cause an upset at a well suited course that favours front runners or those up near the front who can settle near the race pace. If this race is run at pace you'd expect the weight gap to be too big and in that scenario 8.5s looks the good value bet. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator predominently due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Handicapper has given him a chance. Down to a mark of 117. With the jockey taking off a further 7lbs with his claim. 
He's yet to get his head in front in handicap company over hurdles. He did win a handicap over fences however. And looks on a nice enough mark here. Having won that handicap off a 3lbs higher mark than this. 
He's won both runs at this venue. Both over track and trip. The most recent win he won a novice hurdle race in a hack canter. With 17L back to the 2nd placed horse. 
He's got plenty in his favour here. Admittedly the fav looks the one to beat. But I think this lad is a viable alternative should the short fav fluff his lines.

This James Owen trained 5-y-o gelding improved to win his latest hurdle race over two miles on good ground at Southwell nine days ago when easily beating the P Neville trained Brindley by 8 1/2 lengths so with Henry Brooke back in the saddle he can defy his seven pound penalty and follow up today

Init Together has yet to win over hurdles but since being with the Carroll yard has won four times on the flat all weather surface did run well in defeat in Ireland over hurdles so with Luck in running and jumping here today could certainly be involved in the finish

Never Seen Again 7yo who has not had much racing and has been gently reintroduced by new trainer. Done well on both starts and penultimate was over CD where had he settled better at the start he could have been closer. Could well be asked to give it all today and could be enough to get the yards first winner.

KINGSTON BRESIL has a soiund sire for racers under the NH code and this lightly-raced five year old comes from a shrewd yard who know what they are doing. This lowly hurdles mark seems within his reach and with a couple of reappearance sighters behind him he appeals.

OPTICALITY raced well on stable debut from a higher mark in the handicap and has finished fourth in March and May. Couple of runs have been less than impressive but if we catch a going day then there are each-way claims, especially in a weakish looking race. Definitely looks the strongest prospect of those at big prices.

AMBER WAVES has been placed in two races from two starts second in a NH flat race over 2m at Huntingdon on her latest outing in April over hurdles today course distance and going should suit and could well be able to go one better and win this race

the model I run suggests Gordon Grey can win this one. This model result has been driven by Gordon Grey lining up with a comparably high RPR but is not overly penalised for it in the weights. There isn't too much by way of form to go by in this larger 11 horse race but Gordon Grey looks to make an impression after steppnig away for 211 days. Will need to run well fresh to make an impact. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
The Henderson horse will be a short priced fav , but this one may have an each way edge having ran at this c/d on debut when not given a hard race and should be more of a proposition this afternoon.

Only Gordon Grey and BELCAMO have useful hurdling experience and although neither are exposed in this sphere, I just favour the latter for consistency. The Henderson-trained favourite, Twirling, is an above average flat horse over a mile and could be a force if taking to hurdling but its a big IF. Amber waves has had two excellent bumper runs and will also be thereabouts if taking to the jumps too.

Makes his chase debut. Given a mark of 118. With Sean Bowen booked to ride. 
Sean boasts an Incredible 35% win rate when riding hurdlers for this yard. It's always been about chasing with this lad. Making his eagerly anticipated chase bow. 
He's had a couple of runs at this venue. With his close 2nd behind Handlethekettle being the pick of those 2 runs. He ran on very well over the minimum trip. He was a massive eye catcher. 
He won over this trip over hurdles. So we know the trip is no bother. He ran well in his sole P2P run behind De Tellers Fortune. Beaten just 4L by the winner, back in 3rd place. That experience should stand him in good stead for his chase bow.

The model I run suggests Judidee can win this one. Jeudidee lines up here with the second highest RPR of this 7 runner race but has the third lowest weight to carry around this 2m 4f trip. Jeudidee comes into this with some reasonable form having won when last out 29 days ago and three placings in 4 races prior to that. Is a prior course winner and distance winner at another track so clearly knows how to get it done. Looks to marry the two here and get the CD sticker. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator predominently due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Jet Smart is a progressive chaser with strong recent form, winning two of his last three starts. Running off a light weight (10-7) in a competitive Class 3, he looks well-handicapped. At 10/1, he offers excellent each-way value and has solid claims to go close again at Worcester today.

Trainer sends this sole horse to this meeting. A course this horse is familiar with. 
He has to overcome a poor run lto. Personally think he hated the fences. Hence why the yard have quickly reverted back to the smaller obstacles. Looking at his form, it's easy to see why. 
He won his sole run at this track. Beating a useful horse who runs here today called Ballytechno. He made all the running on that occasion. 
He again made all the running on his penultimate run at Taunton. He goes up slightly in trip this time. This distance shouldn't be an issue for him. This is essentially his handicap debut over hurdles. Personally think he's better than this mark. He has a lovely racing weight too. Yard are in form atm.

The model I run suggests Ukantango can win this one. Ukantango lines up jhere with a comparably high RPR but has an official ranking that is considerably lower. This subsequently leaves ukantango going around this 2m 4f trip carrying the least weight of the 7 runner field. Sean Bowen champion jockey picks up the reins for this one in what will be ukantango first ride since a recent wind operation. The hope is the recent wind op aids improvement and sean bowen gets Ukantango over the line first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

TARAHUMARA has won four hurdle races from 2m to 2m 3f third in a hurdle race over 2m 5f at Worcester on his latest outing last month dropped in trip to 2m 4f should suit seems well treated and could well be able to win this race
This none year old was highly tried for the Henry Fry stable might just be revitalised having switched stable and the drop in class and distance one to now

Fine Point ran a solid race over CD on good ground last time and would have been closer if not jumping slightly awkwardly at the second last. He is only a 4yo and will learn and improve. This is a very similar contest and there is no reason to think he will not run well again. A repeat of the run 26 days ago should be enough to see him win.

Pittsburg has been winning while chasing this year with his last win being off an 83 with his lates run chasing being off a 90 to a close second and could take advantage of the lower mark now returning to hurding off an 83

The model I run suggests Stage Show can win the last race of the day. Lines up here with the second highest RPR of the 8 horse race but has an official ranking that leaves him much lower in the weights. This leaves stage show looking to get back in form after a disappointing 9th last time out. this might give the opportunity to do that carrying over a stone less in weight to top weight and current market favourite Star Legend. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Veteran who was not disgraced in their 3 runs last season and is very nicely treated here off dropping mark of 85. Is a C/D winner and good jockey/trainer combination makes current 14/1 solid Ew value here.

Sawgrass produced a breakthrough performance last time out, absolutely bolting up by 13 lengths in a handicap over 1m6f at this very course, clearly showing she relished both the surface and the step up in trip.
Winner over 2 miles in better company than what he's running against today. Back to Class 5 today and could re-ignite his form. Top tier jockey, major sign of intent from his yard.
Golden Handshake made a bit improvement when second up after debut in May and I would expect more today. And while there is no money in the bet he could be a good multiplyer in a Lucky 15

Glint Of Light has had 1 run with no wins or places so far (4th LTO), still very early days in her career. Draw in stall 3 is decent for the trip. Trainer Morrison and jockey Jamin have put her up in trip today, which may suit her stamina better after a 9 length fourth in a 10f maiden LTO. This step up could unlock improvement and the pace looks fair for her style. She is an each way chance if she shows progress but will need to raise her game to threaten a win against this hot fave

Has made late progress in both of her races not being involved but has shown she has some sort of ability both at huge prices. Form from previous races looks pretty strong also and this horse is one to keep on side and I believe could be in the mix
3 times winner who Has not won since December 2023 but did finish a good 3rd on penultimate start. This looks a weak race and if finding the same form has every chance of coming home in front.

Offiahs Boy drops into classified stakes races with every chance of winning. There have been excuses for Offiahs Boy last two races so I won't offer him again if excuses come into places. The conditions of the race make good reading and I thought on reflection this horse would have started favourite and might yet do so. At 7/2 let's go each way as it gives an extra dimension in the race

Glitter Code has been progressive in recent starts, finishing runner-up on his last two outings, including a solid effort when beaten just 3 lengths over 8 furlongs at Nottingham. That performance came off this same handicap mark (60), suggesting he’s on the verge of a breakthrough win.

Due Date is 2 from 2 in classified events. Denied a clear run previously but beaten 1.5 lengths in 3 runs previous to that. This is a weak race and one Due Date should be winning if running to capabilities. NAP
A bad race, which is the best place to put your horse if it is to win. Top on the clock for an in-form yard and ridden by an excellent 7 pound claimer.
Sarabi has a great chance in this race very weak field of and I have this one best off the bunch. If she breaks away smart again I can't see her being out of the top 3

Very close in a class three for MODERN TIMES last time out and with that being so recent, there shouldn't be any reason why he shouldn't be too strong for this level. Justified favourite and if the stable keep him in, will go off much shorter.
El Madar wasn't unduly pushed when chance had gone last time out at Brighton and looks set for a win with course specialist Callum Rodriguez taking the reins.
Worth another chance after disappointing last time. well bred who cost 200k as a yearling, and will be much better than what he has shown so far.
Did okay in debut run when 4 of 8 at Yarmouth at the same distance (6f) this month in what will be similar conditions for today and considering class stays the same, I do think he is over priced.
Looks like a 2 horse race in the opener at Ripon this evening , this one was 3rd on debut bumping into what looks like a good un , and travels from Newmarket and could open its account here.

Duskaura has delivered two promising efforts to date, finishing runner-up on both occasions, including when sent off favourite last time at Catterick??'a sign of strong market confidence. That recent second came after setting the pace and making plenty of use of her natural speed, only being worn down late by a more experienced rival.

Has been a little disappointing in 2 races to date although could be considered a little unlucky last time when denied a clear run. Should be better than those runs have shown and any improvement gives an each way chance.
My Mate Kev was winning for the second time in 5 starts when finishing over 2 lengths clear at Newmarket last month. He is 8lbs higher and up in Class but looks to have a great chance of following up

On Key has shown remarkable consistency at this distance, finishing placed in all 4 starts over the trip, including a close second (beaten just ½ length) on his seasonal reappearance here last time out. That effort suggests he has returned in peak condition, with plenty of scope for further progress.

French Haven has been unlucky in last 2 runs - beaten by a neck and 0.75 lengths. Now steps up in class but will enjoy only having to race with 8st13lb to carry. This rest of this field all have more improvement to seek than this selection based on their previous runs. NB

A beaten favourite in her last 2 starts most recently over the extended mile at Hamilton. Should be suited by the step up in trip being a former course and distance winner off this mark of 59 in August 2024.

Trainer Michael Bell sends Bayadere on the long journey to Ripon and its notable the stable has a good record at the track with its runners and their more fancied runners here, have a 34% winning strike rate.
This filly is still a maiden, had a Wind Op since her last run and returns from an 8 month layoff but I can't see the trainer, sending her here just for the day out.
Although a maiden, she has shown she has ability and starts off this season from a low mark of 67.

4 runs to date and last run was a step in the right diretion when a very good second only bumping into one. I thought she'd go up a few pounds for that , but is in here a pound lower , and bettering that run she must be in with a big shout. Conditons seems the same today and stable still going well. Still EW price to hit the places or win.
Kept on well to go 3rd close to home on the Chelmsford polytrack surface last time out over a furlong further and of interest dropping back to a mile and a half.
Nothing came as close to winning last time in this race as Haptics , going down by a neck at Hamilton. Only up a pound here , can make amends.

An each-way chance is taken on Tim Easterby's Canaria Queen who races of a nine pound lower mark than her last win, way back in April 2024. The 5-y-o showed a hint of a return to form last time out when fourth of thirteen over 6f here three weeks ago. Hopefully the first-time cheekpieces do the trick.

This is the only last time out turf winner in the race and although that was only a Classified and it steps up into a handicap here theres very limited recent turf form among its rivals hence a tip here at a juicy price.

MRS BAGERRAN is a front-runner that hasn't quite been able to make the good starts count recently, but she remains at a rock bottom mark and might be able to make it stick soon. Today's jockey has got her close twice and she's worth backing just in case everything clicks here. There's still place claims anyhow.
